newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak interbank rates ease, seen rising again.
newsitem.headline: Slovak interbank rates ease, seen rising again.

text.p: Slovak interbank rates fell below 20 percent on Monday despite local banks' failure to meet minimum reserves requirements (PMR), for the fifth time this year and the fourth time in a row, dealers said.
The most traded funds on Monday were one-day maturities which hovered at around 12/17 percent bid/offer.
"The rates have fallen as those banks which are short of crowns appear unwilling to accept higher prices," said Martin Hrozany of Credit Lyonnais.
"The decline does not reflect the real market situation, as banks still do not have to quote both sides so some banks just say they would borrow funds at, let's say, 12 percent," Hrozany added.
He said the market's portfolio of state securities remained unbalanced as banks short of liquidity did not have enough securities to use them in the central bank's repo operations.
Traders expect rates to hover at around 20 percent during the next two-week PMR period.

"Another reason for the fall in rates were credit lines among local banks. Tomorrow/next stayed at around 20 and the overnights will return to this level at the beginning of the next PMR period," said Dalibor Cernicka of Bratisava-based Money Market Broker.

Some traders said the artificial market situation with no agreement on rules requiring quotes for both offers and bids could push banks with excessive liquidity to more active participation in finance ministry treasury bill auctions.
Last week the ministry accepted average yield of 13.52 percent in an auction of four-week T-bills. Dealers said they expected similar yields at the next auction of four-week T-bills on Wednesday.
